original_test_intent: Exercise the designated GPU Direct data path between the pinned GPU and BlueField/ConnectX PCIe endpoint with NVQual Test #21 and prove the specified traffic completes with required performance and data integrity, no PCIe/NIC/GPU faults, and no system hang or reboot.
original_method: Bind the GPU UUID/serial/BDF, NIC or DPU serial/port/BDF, complete root-port/switch/retimer/NUMA/IOMMU path and traffic peer; pin the licensed Test #21 configuration, transfer direction, memory-registration mode, payload sizes, queue/stream concurrency, duration and thresholds; drain unrelated traffic, preserve baseline evidence, run once under monitoring, retain raw traffic and health artifacts, and stop on first integrity or platform fault without blind retry.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE supplies the licensed module, stable GPU/NIC/DPU mapping, approved GPUDirect stack and traffic acceptance; an operator drains dependent traffic and owns fault recovery.
required_inputs: Licensed pinned NVQual Test #21 module and compatible GPU, BlueField/ConnectX firmware, drivers, CUDA and DOCA/MOFED stack
GPU UUID/serial/BDF, NIC or DPU serial/port/BDF, traffic peer and complete PCIe/NUMA/IOMMU topology
GPUDirect mode and memory-registration path plus direction, payload, queues/streams, concurrency, duration and repetitions
Throughput, latency, loss, data-integrity, link/AER/NIC/GPU, thermal and power thresholds with aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Dedicated drained SUT and explicit traffic/link-impact authorization
Trusted authenticated access; preserve logs, counters and topology before testing
Do not clear evidence, force reset, change firmware or alter IOMMU/driver/network policy outside the approved recipe
Stop on data mismatch, packet loss above limit, buffer/registration failure, link change, AER/NIC/GPU fault, thermal/power excursion, hang or reboot
agent_execution_scope: Validate stable identities, complete path, stack/configuration, peer, traffic matrix, baselines, limits and interlocks
Run only the approved Test #21 profile on the isolated path
Collect raw throughput, latency, integrity, registration, buffer, PCIe, NIC, GPU and platform evidence
Do not infer targets or limits, reconfigure/reset after a fault, retry automatically or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Test #21 module, GPU-to-BlueField/ConnectX path, GPUDirect mode and traffic matrix
Define data-integrity/performance/error/thermal limits, isolation, aborts and recovery
Review complete evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH GPU DIRECT PCIE TRAFFIC QUALIFICATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind every transfer result to the exact GPU, NIC/DPU, peer, PCIe/NUMA/IOMMU topology, GPUDirect memory-registration mode and traffic profile, and correlate raw data-integrity/performance results with platform health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds stable topology and peer identity, reproducible traffic parameters, quantitative limits, complete telemetry, production isolation, first-fault stop and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic NVQual pass can hide CPU-staged transfers, the wrong GPU/NIC pair, incomplete direction coverage, data corruption, buffer pressure or a recovered link fault.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: GPUDirect traffic can saturate GPU/NIC buffers and shared PCIe/fabric resources, disturb dependent traffic and expose driver, registration, IOMMU or link faults.

project_override_considerations: An equivalent vendor GPUDirect traffic tool may substitute only if it preserves the approved endpoint/path binding, direction and workload matrix, data-integrity checks, quantitative limits and raw evidence. Ordinary NIC throughput or PCIe bandwidth alone does not replace GPU Direct coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approved Test #21 module/license/configuration and authorization
GPU UUID/serial/BDF, NIC/DPU serial/port/BDF, traffic peer and complete PCIe/NUMA/IOMMU path
GPUDirect stack, memory-registration mode, direction, payload, queue/stream, concurrency, duration and acceptance matrix
Complete raw throughput, latency, loss, data-integrity, registration and buffer results with timestamps
Abort/recovery or clean final traffic/link/device state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test #21 Procedure, Criteria and same-row reviews consistently target BlueField/ConnectX PCIe GPU Direct traffic. Missing module, topology, traffic profile and limits are readiness inputs, not conflicting objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The GPU Direct traffic purpose is clear. Licensed tooling, endpoint mapping, stack configuration and acceptance limits are identifiable prerequisites rather than permanent review blockers.

review_improvement: Converts a generic vendor-module pass into a reproducible endpoint- and path-bound GPU Direct traffic qualification with integrity, performance, health and isolation evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A traffic result is meaningful only if data actually traverses the intended direct GPU-to-NIC/DPU path rather than a CPU-staged fallback. Endpoint identity, topology, memory registration and transfer direction therefore must be explicit. Buffer saturation can preserve average throughput while causing loss, retry or corruption, so raw integrity, registration, queue and platform-error evidence is required and the first fault must halt the run before recovery changes state.
